info.title: Time network API
info.description:
Look up blocks, actions and accounts of a Time network, detect deposits, submit signed actions and follow new blocks and payments.

Amounts are decimal strings of microseconds. Heights, nonces and account numbers are decimal strings too.

Answers marked `"source": "index", "proven": false` come from this server's index: a convenience, not a proof. Each carries what is needed to verify it with the SDK and your own trust anchor. Account state is marked `"source": "state_proof"` and carries the proof this server checked.

Unknown or repeated query parameters are refused with 400, so a misspelled filter never returns an unfiltered list. The address of a request is a plain path with an optional query: a fragment, another host, dot segments or backslashes are refused with 400.

A page of another site may read the API only through CORS, from an origin the operator allows: a browser that loads an address under /v1/ for another site as an image, script, style sheet, object, frame or prefetch is refused with 403 `cross_site_refused`. Programs, and people who follow a link, are not affected. A request that carries a body ends its connection with its answer.

Answers that do not depend on the route (an unknown route, another method, a refused origin) are listed under `x-any-request`.

On a network whose genesis has the `market` setting, the routes under `/v1/market` and `/v1/accounts/{id}/market` serve the market of seconds against bitcoin: the book of open orders, the open fills, the trades and the candles. Validators are the only authority. The lists are this server's index of rows the state proved (`market_index.as_of_height` says of which height, `market_index.consistent` whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts); a single order, fill or receiving script comes with its proof, and a wallet reads the row that way before it shows an address to pay. Prices of trades and candles are records of proven payments at the prices of their fills. They are not what a second is worth: no rule of the chain reads them, and two accounts of one person can trade with each other at any price. On any other network these routes answer 404 `no_market`.

x-any-request.description: What a request can be answered with before any route is reached. 403, 414, 421 and 429 are also listed with every route.

400.description: The address is not a plain path with an optional query (`invalid_url`)

405.description: The route exists but does not take this method (`method_not_allowed`); the Allow header names the ones it takes

408.description: The request did not arrive in full within 15 seconds (a body sent too slowly); the answer has no body, and the connection is closed

431.description: The request headers are too large; the answer has no body

get.summary: Network and indexer status

200.description: The network this server follows and how far its index is

get.summary: Health, for monitoring
get.description: 200 while the index keeps up; 503 with reasons when it is behind, failing or stopped. Counts only.

get.summary: This description

200.description: The OpenAPI description of this API

get.summary: The network in figures
get.description: Three parts, each saying what it is. `chain`: the time since the chain started, every second that exists and where it is, the number of accounts and of validators, from the state's own counters read with a proof (identical requests within a second share one read). `activity`: blocks, actions, payments and the seconds they moved, in all, in the last 24 hours and day by day, from this server's index. `holders`: how many accounts hold time and the largest of them, from a count this server makes on a timer; null when it makes none. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two reads of the state under way at once. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

get.summary: Recent blocks
get.description: Newest first by default. The cursor of this list is a height.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A height: blocks below it (order desc) or above it (order asc). A height more than one below the start height of this index is refused with 409 `cursor_below_index_start`.

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given, so a poller keeps its place.

verify.description: How to verify the answer with the SDK and your own trust anchor

get.summary: A block by height
The actions of a block, in block order

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given, so a poller keeps its place.

verify.description: How to verify the answer with the SDK and your own trust anchor

get.summary: What proves a block and its actions, however old
get.description: The state of the network keeps a history of the hashes of its blocks. This reads the rows for this block and the next one with a proof against validator signatures, checks it, and passes it on with the two signed headers of the node. Together with the Merkle proof of `GET /v1/actions/{hash}` that is the receipt `verifyReceipt` of the installed verifier takes: an action of this block can be checked by anyone, against their own trust anchor. The age of a block is no obstacle: its history proof stays when the state drops the block's own rows after fourteen days. Two kinds of block are not provable here. The newest two, which the state does not reach yet: 404 `not_in_history` with a proof of the plain state, whose height shows how far the history reaches; a reader then follows the block by its own signed header (`GET /v1/light-blocks/{height}` and `verifyFastReceipt`), or asks again after two more blocks. And, when the service's node joined the network from a snapshot, blocks at or below the height it was restored at, for which it holds no history: 404 `history_not_held`. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two such reads under way at once: one more is answered 429 `too_many_reads`. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

404.description: `not_in_history`: the state does not reach this block and the next one yet; the proof passed on is that of the plain state (`proof.query` names no block) and shows its height. `history_not_held`: the node of this service holds no history for the block (it joined from a snapshot of a later height); no proof. `not_found`: the node does not have the two signed headers

get.summary: A block as a light client takes it
get.description: The signed header of a block with its validator set and the next one, as the node gives them. Nothing of it is checked here and none of it is this server's word: it is what a light client with its own trust anchor verifies, also when it has to step through older blocks. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two such reads under way at once: one more is answered 429 `too_many_reads`. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

404.description: The node does not have this block

get.summary: Who validates now, and a scheduled upgrade
get.description: The staking row of the current state, read with a proof against validator signatures and passed on with that proof: the validators in force with their voting power, and the sets already announced. `upgrade` is in the answer only when the state was asked about its upgrade row. Identical requests within a second share one read of the state. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two such reads under way at once: one more is answered 429 `too_many_reads`. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

get.summary: An action by its hash
get.description: The hash is the SHA-256 of the signed bytes, as the SDK computes it (`TimeSDK.transactionHash`). The answer holds the decoded action, its bytes (once, as `action.raw`) and the Merkle proof that ties them to the block header. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

market.description: Only for an order (kind 50), a take (kind 52) and a sale to a buy order (kind 53): the row the action made. Its id is not in the action; the chain gives the next one, and the index of the market counts them. It is the index's word: ask the row by this id with its proof (GET /v1/market/orders/{orderid}, GET /v1/market/fills/{fillid}) before acting on it.

made.description: {"order": id} or {"fill": id}. null while the index of the market has not followed the action's block (it follows a block when the next one has come), and on a network without the market.

get.summary: An account by number or name
get.description: The current state is read with a proof against validator signatures and passed on with that proof. Totals come from the index. `state_height` and `indexed_height` stand side by side: the state can be ahead of the index. To conclude that an action is not on the chain, do not combine these two with a 404 received earlier: use the `index.indexed_height` of that 404 itself, or look the hash up after reading the account. And an index says nothing about heights below its start (`index.start_height`). `indexed.state_is_behind` tells when the index already holds an action the account sent in a block above `state_height`, which the proven state does not count: the proven nonce may then be used, and the proof is asked for again. A signer keeps its own count of the nonces it has signed (docs/integration-guide.md, step 3): neither the proof nor the index shows an action that waits for a block. Identical requests within a second share one read of the state. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two such reads under way at once: one more is answered 429 `too_many_reads`. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: The account number, or its name (digits alone are a number; a leading @ forces a name)

404.description: No such account: the proof shows its absence

get.summary: An account with its security settings and stake
get.description: One proof for the account row, its security row (or the proof that it has none), the recoveries under way, its stake and the validator it runs, with the clock the moments of the security row are on (`security_clock`): on a network whose waits survive a stop, compare them with `security_clock.now_elapsed_micros`, not with the time of the state. `GET /v1/accounts/{account}` gives the account row alone, also by name, with the indexed totals. Identical requests within a second share one read of the state. One client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) has at most two such reads under way at once: one more is answered 429 `too_many_reads`. Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

404.description: No such account: the proof shows its absence

get.summary: What an account sent and received
get.description: Actions the account signed (`role` sender), payments it received (`recipient`), and requests for a payment above the daily limit that name it (`pending`: nothing has moved; `request_status` says how the request ended as far as the index knows, and anyone can make such a request for one fee). Newest first by default.

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given, so a poller keeps its place.

verify.description: How to verify the answer with the SDK and your own trust anchor

get.summary: Payments to an account (deposit detection)
get.description:
Payments that moved time to this account when they were included: transfers (kind 3), payments to shops (kind 10, with a reference), payments approved by several keys (kind 73) and completed payments above the daily limit (kind 75) that the index could tie to their request. Oldest first by default, so a poller keeps `next_cursor` and asks again.

A reference does not name its payer: any account whose next nonce matches can pay with it, so more than one payment can carry the same reference. Filter by `from` as well, and credit each hash once.

The list begins at the start height of this index (`index.start_height`) and only grows at its end, so a reader that keeps `next_cursor` misses nothing this index holds. It does miss what lies below the start: a cursor from an index that started earlier is refused (409 `cursor_below_index_start`) and never answered from a later height without a word.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only payments from this account number

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given, so a poller keeps its place.

verify.description: How to verify the answer with the SDK and your own trust anchor

post.description:
Checks the signature and passes the bytes to the node. Nothing is signed here. 202 means the node took it into its waiting list, not that it is in a block.

Before the node is asked, and again whenever it did not take the bytes, the index is asked two things. Are these bytes in a block already? Then the answer is 200 `already_included`. Is another action of this account with the same nonce in a block? Then the answer is 409 `nonce_used` with that action: the same payment signed a second time has another hash, and the node would only say "incorrect nonce". Both look no further than the index has reached.

The signature check proves that the key named in the action signed these bytes, not that the key is one of the account's: that is the node's check. The unsigned relay of bitcoin headers (kind 40) is taken in its one form only, and the kinds of the bitcoin auction (40 to 42, 60 to 62) are refused with 400 `not_on_this_network` on a network whose proven configuration has no auction. Costs 10 from the rate-limit budget.

200.description: These bytes are in an indexed block already

get.summary: Server-sent events: new blocks and payments
get.description:
Events, each with JSON in `data` (shapes under `x-events`): `hello` (once), `payment` (id "<height>.<index>"), `block` (id "<height>", after the payments of that block), `gap` (the heights it names are not sent: too much was missed to send again, or the reader resumes below the start height of this index, which does not hold them; read the lists, from an index that has those heights), `bye` (the server ends the stream: reconnect).

With `account`, only payments to that account are sent (`direction=in`, the default), or from it (`out`), or both. Blocks are always sent.

Reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header or `after` to receive what was missed, up to 256 blocks and 2,000 payments. A stream is ended after a time (15 minutes by default) and when its place is needed; the reader reconnects and loses nothing. Places are counted per IPv4 address or IPv6 /56. When all are taken, a holder with more streams than the one asking gives up its oldest; a stream is not put out in its first seconds, and one that follows an account goes last and never for one that follows none. Streams that follow an account never hold more than four fifths of the places (unless the operator set another share): the rest is kept for readers that follow none. Only addresses the operator has reserved are never put out. Costs 10 from the rate-limit budget.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Only payments of this account number (blocks are always sent)

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: With `account`: payments to it (in, the default), from it (out), or both

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The id of the last event received

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last event received, as browsers send it when they reconnect; `after` takes precedence

200.description: An event stream; the data of each event is described under `x-events`

get.summary: Server-sent events for a wallet: its account was touched at a height
get.description:
For a wallet whose page is open. Events, each with JSON in `data`: `hello` (once), `touch` (a block at `height` included an action that names `account`: sent by it, paying it, or naming it in its security or guardian rules), `bye` (the server ends the stream: reconnect).

A touch is a hint and says so (`"proven": false`): it carries no amount, name, kind or text. On a touch, read the state of the account with a proof (the SDK's getVerifiedState) and show what that says. A false touch leads to nothing new; a missed one costs nothing.

Nothing is kept for a reader: no event has an id, nothing is sent again, and `Last-Event-ID` is not read. A reader that reconnects reads the state of its account. Blocks that the index reaches more than `max_lag_seconds` after they were made are hinted to nobody.

A pool of its own, apart from /v1/stream: places are counted per IPv4 address or IPv6 /56 (16 each by default, 2,000 in all). When all are taken, a holder with more streams than the one asking gives up its oldest; a stream is not put out in its first seconds. A stream is ended after a time (15 minutes by default). Costs 10 from the rate-limit budget.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: The account to follow, by its number

200.description: An event stream; the data of each event is described under `x-events`

get.summary: The market: its rules, its proven summary and the state of its index
get.description: Whether the network has the market, the numbers of its profile, the summary row and the clock of heights with their proof, the Bitcoin header chain as the state proves it, and where this server's index of the market stands. On a network without the market: 404 `no_market`, with the proof of the state that shows it. One client has at most two such reads under way at once (429 `too_many_reads`). Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

404.description: `no_market`: this network has no market; the proof of the state shows its configuration

get.summary: The book of one side, best price first
get.description: Open orders that offer something: `side=sell` by rising price, `side=buy` by falling price, orders at one price by id. `side` is required. An order that is closed or has nothing on offer is not listed here; its owner finds it under GET /v1/accounts/{id}/market. Read an order with its proof (GET /v1/market/orders/{orderid}) before taking it. From the index: `market_index.as_of_height` is the height it is as of, and `market_index.consistent` says whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts. Costs 1.

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Required: the side of the book

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A `next_cursor` of an earlier page of the same side ("<price>.<order>")

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given

get.summary: Both sides of the book, added up by price
get.description: For each of the first `levels` prices of each side: what is on offer, what of it an order can give to a new fill as far as its row says (`takeable_micros`), what all of it costs, and how many orders stand there. At most 5,000 orders of a side are read; `truncated` says when that was not enough. From the index: `market_index.as_of_height` is the height it is as of, and `market_index.consistent` says whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts. Costs 1.

last_recorded_price.description: The price of the fill of the newest proven payment, from the summary the index last proved. Not what a second is worth

get.summary: One order with its proof, or the proof that there is none
get.description: The order row of the current state, read with a proof against validator signatures and passed on with that proof, and whether its owner still stands at that state (the order's key is a spending key of the owner and the owner is not frozen: spec/market.md, 6.10), judged on the owner's account read in the same proof. An order that does not exist (never made, cancelled, or all of it sold and paid) is 404 `order_not_found` with the proof of its absence. One client has at most two such reads under way at once (429 `too_many_reads`). Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

sats.description: What all that is on offer costs

takes_fill.description: As in the list: what the row itself allows

owner_stands.description: From the same proof. `stands` null: the proof does not carry the owner

404.description: `order_not_found`: the proof shows that the state holds no such order; or `no_market`

get.summary: One fill with its proof, or the proof that there is none
get.description: The fill row of the current state with its proof, its order from the same proof, the last Bitcoin height that still counts for it, and whether it can be ended without payment now (`expiry`, the engine's four conditions judged on the proven rows: `TimeSDK.marketExpiry`). `indexed` is the index's word, apart from what is proven: the payments counted for the fill so far and, once it has ended, how. A fill that does not exist (never made, or ended) is 404 `fill_not_found` with the proof of its absence: a payment to its address then is for nothing. One client has at most two such reads under way at once (429 `too_many_reads`). Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

earliest_end_micros.description: The earliest moment it can end without payment whatever the chain learns of Bitcoin, on the clock of the waits

now_elapsed_micros.description: The clock of the waits at this state

expiry.description: `possible`, `reason` (null, or the first condition that fails: halted, height, grace, time), `lastHeight`, `knownMicros`, `earliestEndMicros`, `notBeforeMicros`

404.description: `fill_not_found`: the proof shows that the state holds no such fill, and `indexed.ended` says how it ended if the index saw it; or `no_market`

get.summary: What a receiving script serves, with its proof
get.description: The row of a receiving script in the current state, or the proof that it has none: `free` (no row), `listed` (an order lists it; that order's row says whether a fill uses it), `in_use` (it is the script of an open fill against a buy order) or `used` (a fill that used it has ended: a payment to it now is for nothing, and no order can list it again). One client has at most two such reads under way at once (429 `too_many_reads`). Costs 5 from the rate-limit budget.

get.summary: The recorded trades
get.description: One entry for every accepted proof of payment (kind 54), newest first by default: the fill, its price, the satoshis counted and the seconds bought. The numbers are the rule of the chain applied to the fill's row before the payment (`basis` says whether that row was proven or worked out); `market_index.tape_reconciled` says whether the list adds up to the proven summary, and it is false whenever the list disagrees with the chain. A price here is the price two parties agreed for one fill. It is not what a second is worth. From the index: `market_index.as_of_height` is the height it is as of, and `market_index.consistent` says whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts. Costs 1.

next_cursor.description: Pass it back as `cursor` to continue. When a page is empty it repeats the cursor that was given

get.summary: Candles of recorded trades
get.description: `interval=hour` gives the candles the chain keeps, stored as the state proved them: one for each of its hours with a proven payment (an hour of the chain is 3,600 seconds on a production network and 60 on a laboratory one; `interval_micros` says which), counted from the start of the chain. The other intervals are computed by this index from its list of trades and say so (`source: computed`); their buckets begin on whole multiples of the interval since 1970 (UTC). Newest first; only intervals with a trade are listed; `from` and `to` bound the start of an interval; `next_to` goes back in as `to` for the page before. `interval` is required. A candle is a record of proven payments at the prices of their fills, not what a second is worth: no rule reads it, and it costs little to write. From the index: `market_index.as_of_height` is the height it is as of, and `market_index.consistent` says whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts. Costs 1.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Required: `hour` (the chain's candle) or a computed interval

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Intervals that start at or after this moment, in microseconds since 1970

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Intervals that start at or before this moment, in microseconds since 1970

next_to.description: Pass it back as `to` for the candles before these

get.summary: An account's orders and fills in the market
get.description: The open orders the account owns; the open fills in which it has a part, each with its `roles` (`payer`: it promised the bitcoin; `owner`: its seconds are in the fill; `to`: the seconds go to it); and the fills that ended, newest first, with how each ended as far as the actions say. The chain's own list of an account (`market/account/<id>`, proven by `TimeSDK.marketAccount`) holds the orders it owns and the fills it pays: it misses the seller of a fill against a buy order and the account a fill's seconds go to when another account pays. The index knows both from the rows. At most 200 open fills are listed, newest first (`fills_truncated`); `limit` and `cursor` page the ended ones. From the index: `market_index.as_of_height` is the height it is as of, and `market_index.consistent` says whether the rows held number what the proven summary counts. Costs 1.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: A `next_cursor` of an earlier answer ("<height>.<index>"). A cursor below the start height of this index is refused with 409 `cursor_below_index_start`: it comes from an index that started earlier, and what lies in between is not here.

orderid.name: orderid
orderid.description: The number of an order, from 1

fillid.name: fillid
fillid.description: The number of a fill, from 1

script.name: script
script.description: A receiving script in lower-case hexadecimal: one of the five standard forms (p2pkh, p2sh, p2wpkh, p2wsh, p2tr)

Error400.description: A parameter, the address or the body is not in its accepted form

Error403.description: The request carries an Origin that is not configured (`origin_not_allowed`), or a page of another site makes a browser load an address under /v1/ as an image, script, style sheet, object, frame or prefetch (`cross_site_refused`, judged by the Sec-Fetch-Site, Sec-Fetch-Mode and Sec-Fetch-Dest headers the browser sends)

Error421.description: The Host header names a host this server does not answer under (`unknown_host`)

Error429.description: Too many requests from this address (`rate_limited`), or, on a route that reads a proof or asks the node, this address has its proof reads under way already (`too_many_reads`, two at once unless the operator set another number); see Retry-After

Error503.description: Not available now (`busy`: every place for a read is taken and the wait in line ran out; or the state, the node or the stream places are not available); see Retry-After

NotInIndex.description: Not in the index; `index` says how far the index was

NotTaken409.description: The node already has this action in its waiting list (`already_submitted`), or another action of this account that carries the same nonce is in a block already (`nonce_used`, with `used_by`: `same_content` is true when that action has the same kind and payload: the same payment under another signature, or another payment of the same amount to the same recipient. One hash is one payment: the sender's own records tell which. Verify `used_by.hash` before acting on either answer: it is the index's word)

NotTaken422.description: The node refused the action (`rejected`). If these bytes were sent before, look the hash up before signing anything new

NotTaken502.description: The node did not take the action (`node_unavailable`), or answered for another one (`node_mismatch`)

CursorBelowStart.description: The cursor names a height below the start of this index (`cursor_below_index_start`): the index was rebuilt with a later start height, or the cursor comes from another index. What the chain holds between the cursor and `index.start_height` is not in this index, and the list is not continued from its start without a word. Read those heights from an index that holds them, then go on here without a cursor.

NoMarket.description: `no_market`: this network has no market. From a route that reads the state, the answer carries the proof of the state that shows it

MarketNotReady.description: `market_index_not_ready`: the index has not proven the book yet (`market_index` says where it stands); or the state could not be read. See Retry-After

hash.description: The hash of the submitted bytes

IndexNote.description: How far the index was when it answered

results_checked.description: True once the next verified header committed to a successful result for every action of the block

KindName.description: The name the service's SDK gives the kind (`TimeSDK.KINDS`); null for a kind it does not name, which is stored opaque. 45, `register_protected`, is a registration that creates its account with its keys in their roles and a daily limit (on a network whose genesis has `protected_registration`); like a reveal (2) it has no sender and pays nothing. 50 to 58 (`market_order` … `market_scripts`) are the actions of the market, on a network that has it.

transfers.description: True when including the action moved `amount` to `recipient`

request_hash.description: For a completed payment above the daily limit (kind 75 execute) that the index could tie to its request: the hash of that request

results_checked.description: True once the next verified header committed to a successful result for every action of the block

opaque.description: True for a kind the SDK does not decode: only the envelope is known

fee_rule.description: `market_fee`: the network's fee, paid more than once: by a sell order (kind 50) and by new scripts (58) once more for each script listed, by a proof of payment (54) once more for every 256 bytes of its payload. A list gives no amount for it; GET /v1/actions/{hash} does

fee_micros.description: The fee paid, when the rule and the network fee determine it

unattributed.description: True for a completed payment above the daily limit (kind 75 execute) that the index could not tie to its request: it moved a payment whose recipient and amount the index does not know

role.description: In an account's activity: what the account is to the action. `pending`: a request for a payment above the daily limit names the account; nothing has moved

request_status.description: For a request for a payment above the daily limit (kind 75 request), how it ended as far as the index knows; null for every other action. waiting: nothing has ended it yet. completed, cancelled: by a later action of the sender. dropped: a freeze or a replacement of the sender's keys took it. ended: settled together with other requests, so that it is not known whether it was completed or cancelled. unknown: the index does not follow this sender. The one field of an indexed action that changes after the action is stored. A request costs its sender one fee and moves nothing: never credit one.

ActionProof.description: The Merkle proof that `action.raw` is action `index` of the block, as the node's own lookup gives it. `how` says how to put it in the form the verifier takes.

total.description: The number of actions in the block

root_hash.description: The data hash of the block header, hex

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

indexed_height.description: The height the index had reached when this account was answered. It says nothing about a lookup made earlier: to conclude that an action is not on the chain, use the index.indexed_height of that 404 itself (it must be at or above state_height), or look the hash up after reading the account.

account.description: The account row of the verified state: id, name, balance, nonce, auth_epoch, devices

state_is_behind.description: True when the index holds an action that this account sent in a block above `state_height`: the proven state does not count it. The proven nonce may then be used already: do not sign with it plus one; ask again (the proof follows the chain by one block). Every action the account sent counts, also one that carries no nonce (kinds 72, 73, 74 and 76). False says only that the index, up to `indexed_height`, holds no such action: an action that waits for a block, or one in a block the index has not reached, is in neither. This is the index's word, not part of the proof.

newer_actions.description: Those actions, oldest first. At most 16: when the account has more of them above `state_height`, the list holds the oldest 16, and `last_sent` is still the newest of all.

last_sent.description: The newest action this account sent in a block above `state_height`, also when `newer_actions` does not reach it. When there is none: the action that carries the proven nonce (`account.nonce`). Null if the index holds neither: the account has sent nothing, that action is below the start height of the index or in a block the index has not reached yet (`indexed_height` is below `state_height`), or the nonce was used without an action that carries it (a replacement of the account's keys).

market.description: Where the index of the market stands, on a network that has the market; null on any other, and until a proof has said which it is. It does not change `ok`: watch `consistent` and `tape_reconciled`

PaymentEvent.description: One payment, on the stream and in a webhook: the fields of a list item under the same names

id.description: "payment:<hash>": the same wherever and however often it is delivered

transfers.description: True when including the action moved `amount` to `recipient`

request_hash.description: For a completed payment above the daily limit (kind 75 execute) that the index could tie to its request: the hash of that request

results_checked.description: True once the next verified header committed to a successful result for every action of the block

same_content.description: True when the action that used the nonce has the same kind and payload as the submitted one. That is the same payment signed a second time (a second key, a signer asked twice), or another payment of the same amount to the same recipient: this answer cannot tell the two apart. One hash is one payment: if `used_by.hash` is already the hash of another payment in the sender's records, the submitted one is not made.

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

hash.description: From the proven history of the state
From the proven history of the state

signed_header.description: The signed header of the block as the node gives it, unchecked: the verifier compares it with the proven hash

next_signed_header.description: The signed header of the next block, unchecked in the same way: it commits to the results of this block

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

light_block.description: signed_header, validators and next_validators of the block, as the node gives them: what a light client verifies

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

pos.description: The staking row of the verified state: `active` lists who validates now ({owner, consensus_key, power}), `scheduled` the sets already announced for coming blocks

upgrade.description: The upgrade row of the verified state: a scheduled plan if there is one, null if the proof shows that the state holds none. Present only when the state was asked about the row, which the service does with every state read when its trust manifest says `nodes_report_upgrades: true` (the question in `proof.query` then has `include_upgrade`). When the field is absent the row was not read: that is not "no plan".

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

account.description: The account row of the verified state: id, name, balance, nonce, auth_epoch, devices (its keys, each with can_manage and can_spend)

security.description: The security row of an account that adopted the security rules: policy, frozen_until_elapsed_micros, pending_root, pending_payments, pending_limit. Null: the proof shows it has none

recovery_cases.description: Recoveries by guardians that are under way for this account

stake.description: What the account has staked: positions ({candidate, shares}) and exits that are waiting

validator.description: The validator the account runs, if it is one

genesis_time_micros.description: The start of the network: times in the security row count from it, on the clock `security_clock` gives

security_clock.description: The clock the moments of `security` are on (`ready_elapsed_micros` of what waits, `expires_elapsed_micros` of a waiting replacement, `frozen_until_elapsed_micros`, `allowance_elapsed_micros`), from the same proof. `waits_survive_stops`: whether the network's genesis has that setting. `stopped_micros`: the total of the chain's stops so far, "0" without the setting. `now_elapsed_micros`: the clock at this state, the chain's time since genesis less that total. Compare the moments with it, never with the time of the state: after a stop of the chain they lie before that time and are still to come. A moment as a date is the moment plus `stopped_micros` plus `genesis_time_micros`; with the setting, that is the earliest it can come while it has not come, since a later stop moves it. What keys sign (the expiry of a freeze or of approvals) stays on the chain's time. Null when the state does not carry what the clock is read from.

chain.description: What the state of the chain says of the whole network, read with a proof by this server. Null when no proven state can be read now; `chain_unavailable` then says why.

state_time_micros.description: The time of the proven state

elapsed_micros.description: The time of the proven state less the genesis time

supply_micros.description: Every second that exists: the sum of the four parts. One second is made for each second of the chain, so it equals `elapsed_micros`

staked.description: In the staking pools and on their way out (pos_assets_total)

not_yet_paid.description: The network's bank: new time and fees not yet paid out (bank)

accounts.description: How many accounts the state holds (account_count)

validators.description: How many validators sign the blocks now

activity.description: What this server's index counted, from `counted_from_height`: its word, not a proof.

actions.description: Every action of the blocks, of any kind

payments.description: Actions that moved seconds from one account to another

moved_micros.description: What those payments moved, in micros

actions.description: Every action of the blocks, of any kind

payments.description: Actions that moved seconds from one account to another

moved_micros.description: What those payments moved, in micros

last_24_hours.description: The hour under way and the 23 before it, by block time

days.description: Day by day (UTC), up to the last 30 days to the newest block

actions.description: Every action of the blocks, of any kind

payments.description: Actions that moved seconds from one account to another

moved_micros.description: What those payments moved, in micros

block_interval_ms.description: The average time between two blocks since `counted_from_height`

holders.description: The last count of the accounts that hold time, made by this server every `every_seconds`, account by account with proofs. Null when this server counts none, or before its first count. Only the network's own accounts are shown with a name and a number; every other one is anonymous.

complete.description: False when the network has more accounts than this server reads

holding.description: Accounts that hold more than nothing, on the account or staked

staked_micros.description: In staking pools, valued at what the pool holds, and a validator's own bond

MarketIndexNote.description: Where the index of the market stands. The lists are this index's word; this says how far to rely on them.

as_of_height.description: The orders and fills listed are as the state proved them at this height, or unchanged since their proof. A state is proven by the header of the next block, so when the newest indexed block holds an action of the market this is one below `index.indexed_height` until the next block comes. Null until the book has been proven once

ready.description: The whole book has been proven once. Until then the lists answer 503 `market_index_not_ready`

consistent.description: The rows held number what the proven summary counts (`orders`, `fills`) at `as_of_height`. False while every row is being read again after a difference: rely on the single rows with their proofs meanwhile

pending_rows.description: Rows that the blocks followed so far touched and that are not read again yet: above 0 while a pass is under way, or while reads of the state fail

reading_every_row.description: A reading of every order and fill is under way (the first one, or a repair)

tape_reconciled.description: The list of trades adds up to the proven summary (`trades`, `sats`, `seconds_micros`), its last price is the summary's, every entry has its numbers, no proven fill row has contradicted it and no candle of the chain differs from it. False: the list disagrees with the chain, and the operator's log says where. Null before the first comparison

tape_from_height.description: The first block whose trades the list holds

tape_complete.description: The list of trades begins with the chain. False for an index that started later (`index.start_height` above 1): earlier trades are in the chain's candles only

tape_trades.description: How many trades the list holds

tape_unvalued.description: Entries of the list without numbers: the index did not know the fill or its price when the payment came

tape_faults.description: How often a proven row contradicted the list: a fill whose row was not what the list had counted from, or that ended, or did not end, against what the list says. Above 0, `tape_reconciled` stays false

unread_actions.description: Actions of kinds 50 to 58 that the SDK of this service could not read; after each, every row was read again

waiting_for_indexer.description: The block index is further behind the chain than the node keeps states: rows are read when it has come within reach

MarketMoment.description: A block: its height and its time

MarketOrderRow.description: An order as the state holds it (spec/market.md, 4.1). A sell order has `scripts`; a buy order has `fills` and `forms`.

owner.description: The account that made the order

price.description: Millionths of a satoshi for one second, 1 to 10^15

amount_micros.description: What is still on offer, in microseconds, not counting what open fills hold

bond_micros.description: A buy order: its owner's deposit for what is still on offer

confirmations.description: A sell order: the confirmations its owner asks of every payment. A buy order: the most its owner waits for

pay_blocks.description: The time to pay, in Bitcoin blocks

deposit_ppm.description: A sell order: the deposit a taker locks, in millionths of the amount taken. A buy order: what gave its bond

min_deposit_micros.description: A sell order: the least deposit of a fill

min_sats.description: The smallest trade, in satoshis; also the least a payment of a part may be

open.description: False once the owner cancelled while fills were open: nothing is on offer, and the order goes with its last fill

key.description: The public key that signed the order or last gave it scripts. The order takes a fill only while it is a spending key of the owner

scripts.description: A sell order: its receiving scripts. `fill` while a fill uses the script, `used` once that fill has ended; neither: free

fills.description: A buy order: how many fills are open

forms.description: A buy order: the forms of receiving script its owner can pay to

MarketFillRow.description: A fill as the state holds it (spec/market.md, 4.2): one trade in progress. It shrinks as it is paid: read it again, with its proof, before every payment.

side.description: The side of the order it came from

owner.description: The account whose seconds the fill holds (the seller)

payer.description: The account that promised the bitcoin and locked the deposit

to.description: The account the seconds go to

amount_micros.description: The seconds the fill still holds

sats.description: What is still to pay, in satoshis. Never compute it; read it

script.description: Where the bitcoin must arrive. It serves this fill and nothing else, ever

start_height.description: The best Bitcoin height the chain knew when the fill was made

opened_micros.description: When the fill was made, on the clock of the waits

MarketOrderItem.description: An order in a list: fields of its proven row, and what is counted from them

sats.description: What all that is left costs: ceil(amount_micros × price / 10^12)

pay_blocks.description: The time to pay, in Bitcoin blocks

takes_fill.description: The row itself allows a new fill: it is open, offers something, and has a free receiving script (sell) or a free place among its fills (buy). Not judged: whether its owner still stands (read the order with its proof for that) and whether the Bitcoin header chain is fresh

free_scripts.description: A sell order: receiving scripts that have not served. An order without one takes no fill until its owner gives it new scripts

forms.description: A buy order: the forms of script its owner can pay to

proven_at_height.description: The height of the state that proved this row

MarketEvent.description: What an action of the market did, as the index read it from the action

hash.description: The hash of the action: GET /v1/actions/{hash}

allOf.description: One accepted proof of payment (kind 54): a recorded trade

side.description: The side of the order: `sell` when a taker bought from a sell order, `buy` when a seller sold to a buy order

to.description: The account the seconds went to

price.description: The price of the fill. A record of this trade, not what a second is worth

sats.description: The satoshis counted: what was paid, at most what was still to pay

paid_sats.description: The value of the Bitcoin output

full.description: The payment paid all that was still to pay, and the fill ended

basis.description: What the numbers were counted from: the fill's row as the state proved it before the payment, or that row worked out from the actions since (a second payment before the next proof, or blocks whose state the node no longer held). Null: the fill was not known, and the entry has no numbers

allOf.description: A fill that has ended, and how, as far as the actions say

how.description: `paid`: a proof paid it in full. `expired` (kind 55), `released` by the account its seconds would go to (56), `settled` by the seller (57). `unknown`: the state proved it gone and no indexed action ended it

unpaid_micros.description: The seconds it still held when it ended

MarketBitcoin.description: The Bitcoin header chain the chain follows, from the proven row

fresh.description: Whether a new fill can be made by the freshness rule. The time of the best header is not in the proven row: it is taken from the headers relayed in indexed blocks when the header whose hash is `best_tip` is among the newest of them. Null: not known here

state_height.description: The height of the proven state

rules.description: The numbers of the network's profile and the shared limits (spec/market.md, 2.1), as `TimeSDK.marketRules` gives them: `profile`, `kMin`, `nMin`, `blockMicros`, `graceMicros`, `bondMinPpm`, `minSats`, `hourMicros`, `priceMax`, `satsMax`, `kMax`, `nMax`, `spareBlocks`, `orders`, `payerFills`, `scripts`, `buyFills`

summary.description: The row `market/meta`: `orders` and `fills` count the rows that exist, `next_order` and `next_fill` are the next ids, `trades`, `sats` and `seconds_micros` add up every proven payment, `last_price` is written once one exists

last_recorded_price.description: `summary.last_price`: the price of the fill of the newest proven payment. What was recorded, not what a second is worth

held_micros.description: All the seconds the market holds

heights.description: The clock of heights: when the chain learnt of Bitcoin heights

now_elapsed_micros.description: The clock of the waits at this state

hour.description: The number of the chain's candle this state lies in

number.description: The interval's number: for `hour` the chain's own (its key in the state)

recorded_prices.description: Prices of the fills whose payments were proven in the interval. Records, not a valuation

source.description: `state_row`: the candle the chain keeps, stored as proven. `computed`: added up by this index from its list of trades

matches_tape.description: Only `state_row`: whether this index's list of trades gives the same candle. Null when the list does not begin with the chain's first trade
